questions.question: You are a solution architect evaluating candidate use cases for a Claude-based program. For each scenario, select yes if Claude is appropriate as the primary solution at the architectural level Otherwise, select no.

statements.text: drafting first-pass investigative reports from semi-structured incident logs for analyst review
computing real-time fraud scores at sub-50-millisecond latency on a streaming pipeline
long-context contract review with structured clause extraction and deviation flagging
replacing a vector index for semantic retrieval over a multi-million-document corpus
routing inbound support tickets into 30 categories with reasoning for the chosen routing

questions.explanation: Yes - drafting first-pass reports from semi-structured logs is language synthesis over messy input with a human reviewer downstream, which is a core Claude fit. No - sub-50 ms scoring on a streaming pipeline is below LLM inference latency and is served by a trained scoring model or rules engine. Yes - long-context contract review with clause extraction and deviation flagging exploits exactly the long-context reasoning and structured-output strengths Claude provides. No - a model is not a substitute for a vector index; embeddings plus an ANN store handle retrieval at multi-million-document scale, and Claude sits on top of that retrieval rather than replacing it. Yes - 30-category ticket routing with a stated rationale is classification over natural language where the reasoning trace itself is part of the required output.

questions.question: A managed agent deployment for claims triage has grown from 6 tools to 34 tools over 18 months as product teams added capabilities. Triage accuracy has declined from 91 percent to 78 percent, and average tool selection latency has increased by 2.3 seconds. A junior engineer has proposed adding a tool router agent in front of the current agent to filter the tool list per request. Which two findings should you present to justify capability decomposition before adding the router? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Several tools have not been invoked across the most recent 90 days of traffic.
The proposed router introduces an additional model call on every incoming request.
Tool descriptions overlap across multiple claim categories within the agent's tool set.
The 34 tools serve four distinct claim workflow domains within the triage scope.
The router pattern is well-documented across publicly available agent literature.

questions.explanation: Decomposition is justified by evidence intrinsic to the tool set: overlapping tool descriptions across claim categories (C) cause selection ambiguity, and 34 tools spanning four distinct workflow domains (D) show natural capability seams. A is dead-tool cleanup, B is a cost of the router rather than a decomposition argument, and E is an appeal to popularity.

questions.question: You are reviewing a peer's end-to-end design for a Claude-based platform expected to scale to thousands of concurrent users. For each statement, indicate yes if the statement reflects a sound architectural practice. Otherwise, select no.

statements.text: Authentication and authorization run before retrieval so retrieval can filter by identity.
An asynchronous queue absorbs bursty traffic between intake and the model invocation layer.
Tax computation is encoded directly in the system prompt rather than in code.
Conversation logs include unredacted government identifiers to maximize signal for tuning.

questions.explanation: Yes - resolving identity before retrieval lets access control filter the candidate set so unauthorized content never enters the prompt or the model context, which is the correct enforcement point. Yes - an async queue between intake and model invocation absorbs bursts, smooths load against provider rate limits, and keeps intake responsive under thousands of concurrent users. No - tax computation demands deterministic, auditable arithmetic and belongs in code or a rules engine; a probabilistic model gives no guarantee of correctness or reproducibility. No - storing unredacted government identifiers in conversation logs creates an unnecessary PII exposure across the log store and any downstream tuning pipeline; redact or tokenize at ingestion under data minimization.

questions.question: You are comparing patterns for a batch document-classification job that follows fixed steps: extract metadata, classify, summarize, and persist. Which pattern is the best fit and why?

options.text: A workflow pattern, because the steps are well-defined and predictable per-request token cost is preferred over flexibility.
An agentic pattern, because agents are categorically more accurate than workflows and therefore always preferable regardless of step predictability.
An agentic pattern, because the open-ended planning capability of agents produces more consistent structured outputs than a fixed workflow graph on classification tasks.
A workflow pattern, because agentic patterns do not support tool invocations and therefore cannot execute the persist step that writes results to the downstream store.

questions.explanation: The four steps are fixed and known in advance, so a workflow gives deterministic sequencing, predictable token cost and simpler evaluation. B and C assert agent superiority without basis; D is factually wrong, since agents can invoke tools.

questions.question: A platform team operates a self-hosted multi-agent system on Kubernetes that orchestrates seven specialized agents for invoice processing. The team spends approximately 40 percent of engineering capacity on infrastructure maintenance, message bus reliability, and agent state recovery. The CFO has asked you to evaluate moving to managed agent infrastructure to reclaim engineering capacity. The security officer requires that all customer financial data remain within an approved network boundary. Which factor should most heavily influence your recommendation?

options.text: whether the current seven agents map cleanly to the patterns supported by managed agents
whether managed agents support the current bus topology used by the platform team
whether managed agents reduce per-invoice token costs across the existing processing volume
whether managed agent data handling satisfies the network boundary required by security

questions.explanation: A hard security constraint is a gate, not a trade-off. If managed agent data handling cannot keep financial data inside the approved network boundary, the engineering-capacity savings are irrelevant. The other factors matter only once the boundary requirement is satisfied.

questions.question: You are selecting a pattern for a compliance Q&A assistant that must answer policy questions with citations to the authoritative internal source set. Latency, cost, and audit predictability are prioritized. Which pattern is the best fit?

options.text: multi-agent orchestration with a planner, researcher, and writer agent for every query
a static prompt with the entire policy corpus concatenated into every request
augmented LLM with retrieval-augmented generation over the indexed authoritative corpus and citation rendering on each answer
a pure agent loop with open web-browsing tools to surface the most current policy information, without constraining retrieval to the authoritative internal corpus

questions.explanation: RAG over the authoritative indexed corpus with per-answer citations gives grounded, auditable answers at one model call. Multi-agent orchestration (A) adds latency and cost, full-corpus concatenation (B) is expensive and hits context limits, and open web browsing (D) breaks the authoritative-source and audit requirements.

questions.question: You are a solution architect designing a Claude-based assistant with access to 60 internal tools across multiple business domains. Loading every tool definition on every request increases token usage and time to first response. Which design pattern best addresses this issue without sacrificing capability breadth?

options.text: Use a separate model call to summarize all 60 tool definitions before each user turn.
Apply progressive tool discovery so a curated initial subset is exposed and additional tools are loaded on demand based on the task.
Hard-code a fixed set of five tools per request to reduce token usage, regardless of whether those tools are relevant to the current task.
Increase the maximum context length and load all 60 tool definitions on every request, accepting the higher token cost and latency as necessary for full capability.

questions.explanation: Progressive tool discovery exposes a small relevant subset up front and loads further definitions on demand, cutting prompt tokens and time to first token while keeping all 60 tools reachable. A adds a call and still reads all definitions, C arbitrarily destroys capability, D accepts the cost rather than fixing it.

questions.question: You are sequencing decomposed components in an invoice-processing pipeline. For each of the decomposed components, select the execution layer it belongs to: "Pre-Processing", "Model Stage", or "Post-Processing".

statements.text: Claude-based classification of invoice type
persistence of validated records to the system of record
schema validation of the extracted fields
Claude-based extraction of structured invoice fields
PII redaction on extracted text prior to model invocation
optical character recognition on scanned invoice images

questions.explanation: Model Stage - Claude-based classification of invoice type is model inference. Post-Processing - persistence to the system of record is a downstream action taken on validated output, after the model has returned. Post-Processing - schema validation checks the model's extracted fields and must run on the output, gating persistence. Model Stage - Claude-based extraction of structured fields is model inference. Pre-Processing - PII redaction is explicitly performed on extracted text before the model is invoked, so it prepares the input. Pre-Processing - OCR converts scanned images to text and is the first step that makes the input consumable by the model. The pipeline order reads: OCR, redact, extract, classify, validate, persist.

questions.question: You are reviewing a customer-support agent's configuration. Each candidate tool falls into one of four categories: (1) required to complete defined tasks (2) frequently used and reduces hand-offs (3) occasionally useful for unrelated work (4) speculative future utility Which categories should typically remain in the agent configuration?

options.text: Only category 3, because occasionally useful tools for unrelated work provide broader coverage and should take priority over tools required for the agent's defined tasks.
Categories 1 and 2 only, because they map to defined tasks and the agent's regular hand-offs.
All four categories, because broader tool access is categorically better for agent performance regardless of whether the tools map to defined tasks or regular hand-offs.
Only category 4, because speculative future-utility tools provide the most flexibility and should be configured even when no defined task currently requires them.

questions.explanation: Least privilege for tools: keep what the defined tasks require (category 1) and what materially reduces hand-offs in the agent's own scope (category 2). Occasional unrelated tools (3) and speculative tools (4) enlarge the selection space, dilute tool descriptions and add attack surface for no defined benefit.

questions.domain: Claude Models, Prompting and Context Engineering
questions.question: You are classifying token-management tactics by where in the request lifecycle each tactic applies. For each of the tactics, select where in the request lifecycle each tactic applies: "Input Preparation", "Prompt Construction", or "Output Handling".

statements.text: Persist the validated output for downstream consumption and audit.
Order the prompt sections so cacheable content sits before per-request content.
Summarize prior conversation history when full history is no longer needed.
Validate the model's structured output against the expected schema.
Move stable repeated content into a cacheable prefix at the head of the prompt.
Trim retrieved passages to spans relevant to the user's question.

questions.explanation: Output Handling - persisting validated output for downstream use and audit acts on what the model returned. Prompt Construction - ordering sections so cacheable content precedes per-request content is an assembly decision that determines how much of the prefix can be cached. Input Preparation - summarizing prior conversation history compresses material before it enters the request. Output Handling - schema validation checks the returned structure and drives any retry. Prompt Construction - moving stable repeated content into a cacheable prefix at the head of the prompt is prefix layout. Input Preparation - trimming retrieved passages to the relevant spans reduces what is fed in, before assembly.

questions.domain: Claude Models, Prompting and Context Engineering
questions.question: You are reviewing a peer's draft system prompt that contains contradictory instructions: one section says to never speculate beyond the supplied source, and another says to confidently fill in any gaps. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Add a priority-ordering instruction that tells the model to evaluate all available instructions and apply the most contextually appropriate one on each request.
Increase the temperature setting so that output randomness masks the contradictions.
Resolve the contradiction by removing or rewording the gap-filling instruction so the prompt consistently constrains the model to source-supported content.
Keep both contradictory instructions in place and rely on the model to select which one to follow on each individual request, accepting inconsistent behavior as a result.

questions.explanation: Contradictory instructions produce non-deterministic behaviour. The fix is to resolve the conflict in the prompt itself so it consistently constrains the model to source-supported content. A and D delegate the conflict to the model; B misuses temperature and does not remove the contradiction.

questions.domain: Claude Models, Prompting and Context Engineering
questions.question: A document analysis service processes legal filings averaging 80,000 tokens each. Each filing is queried by attorneys an average of 14 times during a case. The current architecture sends the full filing on every query. The CFO has asked you to reduce per-query costs while preserving response quality. The security officer requires that filing contents not be stored outside Fabrikam's tenancy. Which optimization approach should you recommend?

options.text: Summarize each filing once at intake and run all subsequent queries against the summary.
Move the workload to a smaller Claude model to reduce the per-token cost paid.
Cache the filing as the prompt prefix for reuse across the 14 queries per case.
Index filings in a vector store and retrieve only the relevant passages per query.

questions.explanation: The filing is re-queried ~14 times, so caching it as a static prompt prefix makes the repeated 80k tokens cheap on every subsequent query while preserving full fidelity and keeping content inside the tenancy. A loses detail the attorneys need, B trades quality for cost, D adds an external index and risks missing context for whole-document questions.

questions.question: You are classifying chunking strategies by the corpus type each is best suited to. For each chunking strategy, select where in the request lifecycle each applies: "Long Structured Documents", "Heterogeneous Short Records", or "Code or Hierarchical Specs".

statements.text: function-level or section-level chunking for code modules
tree-aware chunking that follows code or specification hierarchy
per-record chunking where each record is one chunk
semantic chunking along clause or paragraph boundaries
fixed-size chunking with overlap for short records of similar length
hierarchical chunking that mirrors document section structure

questions.explanation: Code or Hierarchical Specs - function-level chunking keeps each callable unit intact with its signature, which is the natural boundary in code modules. Code or Hierarchical Specs - tree-aware chunking follows the AST or specification hierarchy so children stay attached to their parent context. Heterogeneous Short Records - each record is already self-contained, so one record per chunk avoids merging unrelated entries. Long Structured Documents - clause and paragraph boundaries are the semantic units in contracts, policies and reports. Heterogeneous Short Records - fixed-size chunking with overlap is a reasonable fit only when the records are short and of similar length, as stated. Long Structured Documents - hierarchical chunking mirroring section structure preserves the heading context a long document depends on for retrieval.

questions.domain: Claude Models, Prompting and Context Engineering
questions.question: You are designing the prompt for a ticket-triage classifier with thirty well-defined categories and clear category descriptions in the prompt. Which technique is most appropriate as the starting point?

options.text: a prompt that demands the model invent new categories when the supplied ones do not fit
a chain-of-thought prompt for a routing decision that does not require multi-step reasoning
a zero-shot prompt that specifies the categories with their descriptions and the required output format
a prompt with no category descriptions, expecting the model to infer the category set

questions.explanation: With thirty well-defined categories and clear descriptions available, a zero-shot prompt that states the categories and the required output format is the right starting point; add examples only if evaluation shows gaps. B adds latency for a decision that needs no multi-step reasoning, A and D remove the defined label set.

questions.question: You are evaluating retrieval-strategy claims used by a peer team. For each claim, select yes if the statement is generally accurate. Otherwise, select no.

statements.text: Dense vector retrieval is well suited to recovering paraphrased intent against unstructured text.
Sparse term-matching retrieval recovers exact terms (such as identifiers and rare tokens) more reliably than dense alone.
Structured query retrieval is the right fit for filter-and-aggregate workloads against a relational store with schema and indexes.
Hybrid retrieval is identical to dense-only retrieval and shares the same recall characteristics.
Random sampling of a data store is a sound retrieval strategy for production Q&A.

questions.explanation: Yes - embeddings capture semantic similarity, so dense retrieval matches paraphrased intent where the query shares no surface terms with the passage. Yes - sparse methods such as BM25 match tokens literally, which is why rare identifiers, part numbers and error codes are recovered more reliably than by dense retrieval alone. Yes - filter-and-aggregate work over a relational store with a schema and indexes belongs in SQL, not in an approximate similarity search. No - hybrid combines dense and sparse signals precisely because their recall profiles differ; if it were identical to dense-only there would be no reason to run it. No - random sampling has no relationship to the query and cannot reliably surface the passages an answer depends on.

questions.domain: Claude Models, Prompting and Context Engineering
questions.question: You are designing a content moderation classifier that processes high volumes of user-generated comments under a tight per-message latency budget using well-defined classification labels. Which model selection best aligns with the workload?

options.text: Sonnet with extended thinking enabled, because deeper reasoning should be applied to every moderation request to improve edge-case handling.
Sonnet, because larger general-purpose models are preferred even when workload latency requirements are strict.
Opus, because every moderation decision requires maximum reasoning depth regardless of classification complexity.
Haiku, because its latency and cost profile align with high-volume classification workloads that require limited reasoning depth.

questions.explanation: High volume, tight per-message latency and well-defined labels is the canonical Haiku profile. Extended thinking (A) and heavier tiers (B, C) add latency and cost without a reasoning requirement that justifies them.

questions.domain: Claude Models, Prompting and Context Engineering
questions.question: You are evaluating prompting claims in a peer's design document. For each claim, select yes if the claim reflects sound practice. Otherwise, select no.

statements.text: Zero-shot is appropriate as a starting point for closed-set classification when categories and descriptions are provided in the prompt.
Adding a few-shot example set with exact field names anchors output formatting on extraction tasks.
Chain-of-thought should be the default on every task regardless of complexity.
Leading-question framing is best mitigated by asking for an even-handed comparison with stated criteria.
Behavioral differences across model versions can be ignored once a prompt has been validated on one version.

questions.explanation: Yes - with a closed category set and descriptions already in the prompt, zero-shot is the right starting point; add examples only where evaluation shows gaps. Yes - few-shot examples using the exact field names anchor the output shape and reduce formatting drift on extraction tasks. No - chain-of-thought adds latency and tokens, and on simple routing or classification it brings no accuracy benefit; reserve it for genuinely multi-step reasoning. Yes - a leading prompt biases the answer toward the framing, so requesting an even-handed comparison against stated criteria is the correct mitigation. No - behaviour shifts across model versions, so prompts must be re-validated against the evaluation set on each upgrade rather than assumed stable.

questions.domain: Claude Models, Prompting and Context Engineering
questions.question: You are evaluating model-selection claims used by a peer team. For each statement, select yes if the statement is generally true. Otherwise, select no.

statements.text: Heavier-reasoning models typically consume more of the rate limit and run more slowly than lighter models on the same input.
A representative-sample evaluation on the target workload is the right basis for confirming a model selection.
The most capable model is always the right choice regardless of the workload profile.
Tiered routing can serve routine traffic with a lighter model while reserving a heavier model for traffic that needs its capability.
Selecting a model based on which version was most recently announced is the right basis for production decisions.

questions.explanation: Yes - heavier models generate more slowly and draw more against token-based rate limits for the same input, which is why latency-sensitive high-volume workloads favour lighter tiers. Yes - confirming a selection requires running candidates against a representative sample of the actual workload, not published benchmarks. No - capability is only one axis; latency tolerance, volume and cost ceiling matter, and the correct rule is the lightest model that clears the quality bar. Yes - tiered routing by task complexity is a standard pattern that keeps cost and latency down on routine traffic without giving up capability where it is needed. No - recency of announcement says nothing about fit for a given workload; a new version is a trigger to re-evaluate, not a reason to adopt.

questions.domain: Claude Models, Prompting and Context Engineering
questions.question: You are selecting a model for a new production workload and must complete the upstream steps before testing candidate models empirically. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE running a representative sample on a candidate model? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Sign off the production rollout plan with the platform and security teams.
Select the lightest model that consistently meets the quality bar across the sample.
Choose a candidate model based on the requirements profile and known capabilities.
Retest the model choice when a new model version becomes available.
Define the quality bar, latency tolerance, and expected volume for the workload.

questions.explanation: Before empirical testing you need the requirements profile: the quality bar, latency tolerance and expected volume (E), and a candidate model chosen against that profile and known capabilities (C). B is the outcome of testing, A is rollout, D is ongoing re-evaluation.

questions.question: You are investigating an MCP server that fails on first launch but succeeds on subsequent runs. The system permission dialogs appeared on first launch. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Recognize the first-run permission grant as the cause, document the expected behavior in onboarding guidance, and confirm that subsequent runs succeed.
Disable operating system permission dialogs entirely, accept the resulting security implications, and proceed without confirming whether the failure recurs.
Reinstall the operating system to clear all permission state, and do not first confirm whether the one-time permission grant was the actual cause of failure.
Treat the first-run failure as a permanent fault, replace the MCP server with an alternative implementation, and do not verify whether subsequent runs succeed.

questions.explanation: First-run OS permission dialogs are a known one-time grant; the correct response is to recognise the cause, document it in onboarding and verify subsequent runs succeed. B trades away security, C is disproportionate, D discards a working component without diagnosis.

questions.question: You are compiling factors that should drive the choice between Model Context Protocol (MCP), direct API integration, and agent-to-agent handoff. Which two factors belong on the list? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: whether the underlying transport supports encryption in transit between the integrated services
whether the interaction is stateless and latency-sensitive or stateful and longer-running
whether the vendor publishes detailed reference documentation for each candidate protocol
whether the team has prior implementation experience with any of the candidate protocols
whether the integration must be portable across multiple AI clients in the ecosystem

questions.explanation: Protocol choice is driven by interaction shape — stateless and latency-sensitive versus stateful and long-running (B) — and by whether the integration must be reusable across multiple AI clients, which is exactly what MCP provides (E). A applies to all options, C and D are team/vendor conveniences rather than architectural drivers.

questions.question: You are selecting a protocol for a single low-latency stateless tool call from a Claude-based assistant to an internal pricing service that already exposes a stable HTTP API. Which integration mechanism is the most appropriate?

options.text: a bespoke streaming protocol layered over an unrelated asynchronous message bus
an agent-to-agent handoff that introduces another Claude-based agent in front of the pricing service
a long-lived stateful session protocol for a stateless single-call interaction
a direct API call to the existing endpoint with the appropriate scoped credentials

questions.explanation: A single stateless low-latency call to an existing stable HTTP endpoint is best served by a direct API call with scoped credentials. MCP-style session protocols (C), an extra agent hop (B) or a bespoke bus (A) add latency and moving parts for no benefit.

questions.question: You are assessing a Claude-based system whose dominant risk is silent quality drift on safety relevant outputs after a model-version upgrade. Which assessment activity most directly addresses this risk?

options.text: Disable adversarial evaluation entirely during model-version upgrade cycles to reduce evaluation cost, accepting that safety drift will go undetected until it appears in production.
Skip evaluation on each model-version upgrade and rely on user-submitted complaints to surface safety drift after the upgraded model has already served production traffic.
Rotate adversarial inputs randomly so no two upgrades are scored on the same set.
Maintain an adversarial evaluation set with version-attributed scoring so each upgrade is measured against the same set before promotion.

questions.explanation: Silent drift is detected by scoring every version against the same stable adversarial set, with results attributed per version and checked before promotion. C destroys comparability, A and B remove detection entirely.

questions.question: You are designing a human-in-the-loop validation workflow. Which two design elements belong in the workflow? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: capture of reviewer decisions as labeled data that feeds the evaluation set over time
mandatory reviewer agreement with the model output to maintain consistent reviewer-model alignment
aggregate reviewer throughput metrics published weekly to leadership for headcount planning
uniform sampling of all model outputs to give every request an equal chance of review
risk-stratified sampling that concentrates reviewer attention on low-confidence and high-impact outputs

questions.explanation: Risk-stratified sampling (E) puts reviewer capacity where impact and uncertainty are highest, and capturing reviewer decisions as labelled data (A) compounds into the evaluation set over time. B destroys the point of independent review, C is a management metric, D spreads scarce review capacity uniformly.

questions.question: You are designing a test strategy for a Claude-based pipeline that handles sensitive financial data. Which two test types should be prioritized to cover both safety-under-attack and cross-component correctness? (Choose two.)

options.text: integration tests that verify end-to-end pipeline behavior across all components
unit tests targeting individual prompt-template rendering logic only
adversarial tests using prompt-injection and malformed-input cases
smoke tests to verify core paths after each deployment
regression tests against a stable reference set of previously known good outputs

questions.explanation: Adversarial tests with prompt-injection and malformed inputs cover safety-under-attack (C); integration tests covering end-to-end behaviour across components cover cross-component correctness (A). B is too narrow, D and E are valuable but address neither dimension specifically.

questions.question: A Claude-based research assistant begins producing responses that confidently contradict its retrieved source documents despite no change to the retrieval pipeline. Which two diagnostic actions most directly identify the root cause of this behavior? (Choose two.)

options.text: Switch the retrieval index to a denser embedding model to improve chunk relevance scores.
Isolate whether the failure reproduces on the previous model version to test for model mismatch.
Inspect system-prompt grounding instructions to determine whether citation constraints remain intact.
Reduce the temperature setting to lower response variance across all query types.
Increase the context window size to allow more retrieved chunks per query.

questions.explanation: The retrieval pipeline is unchanged, so the likely causes are upstream of retrieval: a model-version change (B, reproduce on the previous version) or weakened grounding/citation constraints in the system prompt (C). A, D and E are speculative tuning changes that do not isolate a cause.

questions.question: A pilot AI assistant for procurement specialists shows 89 percent first-response acceptance, but follow-up surveys reveal that specialists frequently override the assistant's vendor recommendations after consulting unrelated criteria the assistant did not consider. The pilot owner wants to ship the assistant as is, given the strong acceptance rate. Which two discernment-competency observations should you raise BEFORE approving the launch? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Acceptance does not measure whether recommendations are right after specialist review.
The survey response rate may not be statistically representative of all the specialists.
The unconsidered criteria represent a scope gap in the assistant's input space directly.
The acceptance rate alone is sufficient evidence of readiness for general production use.
The pilot duration was likely too short to establish reliability across the full year.

questions.explanation: Acceptance of a first response is not a correctness measure once specialists later override it (A), and the criteria the assistant never saw are a genuine input-scope gap (C). D restates the flawed reasoning; B and E are generic survey/duration caveats rather than discernment findings.

questions.question: The platform team at Trenova Systems, Inc. needs to reduce per-query cost and p95 latency for a high-volume Claude pipeline without degrading output quality on the core use case. Which two optimizations directly target both cost and latency simultaneously? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add a retrieval step that fetches the full source corpus into the context window before generation.
Expand the system prompt to include additional few-shot examples for every request.
Increase max_tokens to reduce the frequency of truncated responses requiring follow-up calls.
Enable prompt caching on the static system-prompt prefix to reduce billable input tokens on repeated calls.
Route straightforward query types to a smaller, faster Claude model and reserve the full model for complex cases.

questions.explanation: Prompt caching on the static prefix (D) cuts billable input tokens and prefill time; routing simple queries to a smaller model (E) cuts both price per token and generation latency. A, B and C all add tokens or work.

questions.question: After a prompt template update, several previously passing test cases now produce unexpected outputs. Which test type is specifically designed to detect this category of failure?

options.text: regression tests scored against a stable reference set of known-good behavior
adversarial tests that probe for prompt-injection vulnerabilities
integration tests that validate cross-component pipeline behavior
smoke tests that confirm high-level system availability after the change

questions.explanation: Regression tests scored against a stable known-good reference set exist precisely to catch behaviour changes introduced by a prompt or template edit. The other test types target injection, cross-component wiring and availability.

questions.question: You are integrating human review into a high-volume classification pipeline where reviewing every output is infeasible. Which sampling strategy best balances throughput with quality oversight?

options.text: no sampling at all, relying entirely on user-submitted complaints to surface quality and safety issues after they have already affected end users at scale
risk-stratified sampling that reviews all low-confidence and high-impact outputs and a smaller random sample of high-confidence routine outputs
inverse sampling that reviews only high-confidence routine outputs and skips all low-confidence and high-impact outputs
universal sampling that reviews every output regardless of confidence level or throughput impact, treating all outputs as equally requiring human review

questions.explanation: Risk-stratified sampling reviews all low-confidence and high-impact outputs plus a smaller random sample of routine high-confidence ones, giving oversight where it matters within a feasible review budget. A has no oversight, C inverts the priority, D is infeasible at volume.

questions.question: You are rolling out monitoring for a Claude-based deployment and must complete the specification steps before instrumenting the deployment. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE instrumenting the deployment to emit metrics and traces? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Document the dashboards, alerts, and runbooks for the on-call rotation that will respond.
Build the dashboards that surface metrics across slices at the cadence the team operates on.
Define the service-level objectives (SLOs) and the error budgets the deployment will be held to.
Tune the alert thresholds based on observed normal-state distributions to reduce false positives.
Define the metrics and the slices the deployment will monitor across normal and adversarial traffic.

questions.explanation: Instrumentation must be specified before it is built: define the SLOs and error budgets the deployment is held to (C), and the metrics and slices to be emitted across normal and adversarial traffic (E). Dashboards, alert tuning and runbooks (A, B, D) come after telemetry exists.

questions.question: You are an architect supporting the iteration phase of a deployed Claude-based system. Which activity most directly fits this phase?

options.text: Discard the evaluation framework and reference set once the deployment is in production, accepting that future iterations will have no structured basis for measuring the impact of changes.
Rebuild the entire system architecture from scratch at the start of every iteration cycle regardless of what production telemetry, evaluations, and stakeholder feedback indicate is needed.
Review production telemetry, sampled output evaluations, and stakeholder feedback to identify the highest-impact change for the next cycle, then plan the change against the evaluation framework.
Stop measuring production outcomes once the deployment has successfully launched, treating the go-live milestone as the end of the evaluation and iteration cycle.

questions.explanation: Iteration means reviewing telemetry, sampled output evaluations and stakeholder feedback, picking the highest-impact change, and planning it against the existing evaluation framework. A and D discard measurement; B discards continuity.

questions.question: A Claude architect at a health services organization is defining evaluation metrics for a clinical-summary pipeline. The pipeline must remain within a per query cost ceiling and must never surface patient data to unauthorized roles. Which two metrics directly address these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: role-based access-control enforcement rate measured on a red-team dataset
response latency at the 95th percentile across a one-week sample window
BLEU score computed against a human-annotated reference summary set
throughput measured as successful requests processed per minute
per-query token cost measured against the defined cost ceiling

questions.explanation: Per-query token cost against the defined ceiling (E) maps to the cost requirement; RBAC enforcement rate measured on a red-team dataset (A) maps to the never-surface-PHI-to-unauthorised-roles requirement. B, C and D measure other properties.

questions.question: A revenue projection assistant has missed its monthly cost target by 38 percent. Profiling shows three contributors: a 6,000-token policy preamble repeated on every call (45 percent of cost), retrieval of historical sales chunks averaging 3,000 tokens per call (30 percent), and inference on a flagship tier model (25 percent). Stakeholders require that projection accuracy remain unchanged. Which two optimizations should you sequence first to reduce cost without affecting accuracy? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Cache common retrieved sales chunks accessed across many of the daily queries.
Truncate the policy preamble to remove non-essential clauses from the prompt.
Enable prompt caching on the static policy preamble across the recurring calls.
Switch the workload to a smaller, faster Claude model tier across all queries.
Reduce the number of historical sales chunks retrieved across each query run.

questions.explanation: Only caching reduces cost without touching what the model sees: prompt caching on the static 6,000-token preamble (C) targets the largest contributor, and caching commonly retrieved sales chunks (A) targets the second. B, D and E all change prompt content, retrieval depth or model tier, which risks the fixed accuracy requirement.

questions.question: You are operating an interactive assistant whose dominant performance constraint is per-turn latency. Quality on routine turns is already acceptable. Which configuration adjustment most directly improves latency without disproportionately damaging quality?

options.text: Reduce retrieval depth to the top-k passages that historically cover the answer, and cache stable system-prompt content.
Increase retrieval depth to the corpus maximum to improve recall regardless of latency.
Disable prompt caching entirely to ensure fresh context processing on every request, preventing stale prefix content from affecting latency-sensitive interactions.
Switch every turn to the heaviest available model to maximize output quality, accepting that the increased model latency will worsen the per-turn SLO rather than improve it.

questions.explanation: Trimming retrieval to the top-k that historically covers the answer reduces prefill tokens, and caching the stable system prefix removes repeated prefill — both cut latency with minimal quality cost on already-acceptable routine turns. B, C and D all increase latency.

questions.question: You are evaluating an evaluation set used to score a Claude-based hiring-support tool. The set is drawn from one geographic region and one tenure band. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Expand the evaluation set to cover the geographic regions and tenure bands the tool will serve, and rescore the system on the expanded set before broader release.
Continue using the narrow evaluation set drawn from one region and one tenure band because the existing benchmark scores are already high on that subset.
Reduce the evaluation set further to a single demographic subgroup to simplify score interpretation, narrowing coverage rather than expanding it to match the intended user population.
Discard all quantitative evaluation and replace it with qualitative impressions collected from a small, convenience-selected group that may not represent the tool's full user population.

questions.explanation: An evaluation set drawn from one region and one tenure band cannot support claims about the population the tool will serve; expand coverage to the intended slices and rescore before broader release. B keeps a biased benchmark, C narrows further, D discards measurement.

questions.question: You are reviewing instrumentation in a multi-agent system. Which two findings constitute valid observability gaps in the instrumentation? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Model identity and version on each turn are not recorded with the turn artifacts.
Tool-call payloads and outcomes are recorded with redaction applied to known sensitive fields.
Latency and token usage on every span are emitted to the central metrics pipeline.
Request-scoped correlation identifiers do not propagate across agent and tool calls.
Trace spans for each agent step are exported to the shared distributed-tracing backend.

questions.explanation: Missing model identity and version per turn (A) makes drift and incident attribution impossible; correlation IDs that do not propagate across agent and tool calls (D) break end-to-end tracing. B, C and E describe instrumentation that is present and correct.

questions.question: You are building an evaluation pipeline for a Claude-based deployment and must complete the specification steps before running the deployment against the dataset. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE running the deployment against the evaluation dataset? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Score the deployment outputs against the reference labels and aggregate the metrics.
Publish the aggregated metrics to a dashboard and gate releases on threshold checks.
Review failure cases with subject matter experts to refine the scoring rubric.
Define the metrics and slices the framework will report across representative, edge, and adversarial cases.
Curate and label the evaluation dataset to match the defined slices.

questions.explanation: Specification precedes execution: define the metrics and slices across representative, edge and adversarial cases (D), then curate and label the dataset to match those slices (E). A, B and C all happen after the run.

questions.question: You are identifying the highest-impact optimization for a deployment whose token cost is dominated by a long, repeated system prompt and a large retrieved context per request. Which optimization most directly targets the dominant cost driver?

options.text: Add additional repeated content to the system prompt to give the model more guidance.
Increase retrieval depth on every request to maximize recall, worsening the dominant cost driver by adding more retrieved tokens per request rather than reducing them.
Switch every request to the heaviest available model to maximize output quality, accepting that higher per-request inference cost compounds rather than addresses the dominant cost driver.
Move the long, repeated system prompt into a cacheable prefix and trim retrieved context to the spans relevant to each query.

questions.explanation: The two dominant drivers are the repeated system prompt and oversized retrieved context, so move the prompt into a cacheable prefix and trim retrieval to the relevant spans. A, B and C each enlarge the dominant driver or the per-request inference cost.

questions.question: An operations engineer reports that a Claude-based pipeline began returning malformed JSON responses after a scheduled maintenance window, causing downstream processing failures. Which two investigative steps most directly isolate the root cause? (Choose two.)

options.text: Compare the current system prompt and output schema configuration against the last known good version from before the maintenance window.
Switch to a different Claude model tier to rule out provider-side changes as a contributing factor.
Increase the max tokens limit to determine whether output truncation is causing incomplete JSON structures.
Replay a set of premaintenance requests against the current configuration and inspect the raw model output before downstream parsing.
Clear the prompt cache and resubmit all pending requests to eliminate stale cached prefixes.

questions.explanation: Something changed in the maintenance window, so diff the current system prompt and output-schema configuration against the last known-good version (A) and replay pre-maintenance requests while inspecting raw model output before parsing (D). B, C and E are remediation guesses that do not isolate the change.

questions.question: You are running a controlled experiment to compare two prompts and must complete the design steps before executing the experiment. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE running the experiment with random assignment? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Analyze the results against the predefined success metric and significance threshold.
Determine the minimum detectable effect size and the sample size needed for power.
Document the recommendation, the trade-offs accepted, and the alternatives considered.
Decide whether to promote, reject, or iterate the candidate based on the analysis.
Define the hypothesis and the primary success metric for the comparison.

questions.explanation: Experiment design comes first: state the hypothesis and primary success metric (E), then determine the minimum detectable effect and the sample size needed for power (B). A, C and D are post-execution steps.

questions.question: An architect is reviewing a Claude-based candidate-screening tool prior to deployment. A stakeholder asserts that because the model was not trained on company data, no bias evaluation is necessary. Which two responses most accurately challenge this assertion? (Choose two.)

options.text: The model may carry demographic biases from pretraining that manifest in screening outcomes regardless of fine-tuning.
Transparency obligations are satisfied by disclosing that an AI system is in use, without further evaluation.
The system should be evaluated on outcome-disparity metrics across protected groups before deployment.
Fairness testing is required only when the training dataset is known to contain protected-class labels.
Bias evaluation is unnecessary when the model provider has published a responsible-use policy.

questions.explanation: Pretraining bias can surface in screening outcomes regardless of whether company data was used for training (A), so the system needs outcome-disparity testing across protected groups before deployment (C). B, D and E all restate the assertion being challenged.

questions.question: You are building an ethics review checklist for deployments supported by artificial intelligence (AI). Which two checks belong on the list? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Verify that outputs do not rely on generalizations about people that the underlying data does not support.
Confirm that vendor licensing terms permit the planned production use of the model.
Confirm that latency and throughput targets are met across the supported user populations.
Restrict the ethics review to outputs that exceed a defined model-confidence threshold.
Confirm that high-impact decisions retain human accountability rather than being attributed to the model.

questions.explanation: Ethics checks: outputs must not rest on unsupported generalisations about people (A), and high-impact decisions must retain named human accountability (E). B is legal/licensing, C is performance, D would exclude exactly the low-confidence outputs that need review.

questions.question: You are defining where human review must remain in a planned automated pipeline. Which placement reflects sound human-in-the-loop design?

options.text: Remove all human review steps from the pipeline to maximize throughput, accepting that high-impact and irreversible actions will be taken without any human approval or oversight.
Place a human reviewer in the loop for a randomly selected sample of requests, without defining criteria for what the reviewer should check or which output categories require mandatory review.
Place a human reviewer between the model's output and any high-impact, irreversible action, with explicit criteria for what the reviewer must check before approval.
Place a human reviewer only after the irreversible action has already executed, making the review a post-hoc audit rather than a meaningful pre-action check or approval gate.

questions.explanation: Place the reviewer between the model output and any high-impact irreversible action, with explicit criteria for what must be checked before approval. A removes oversight, B is unstructured, D reviews after the damage is done.

questions.question: An engineer inadvertently commits an API key to the repository by placing it in .claude/settings.json. Which configuration design principle was violated?

options.text: Project-scope configuration should always override user-scope configuration.
MCP server definitions must reside in environment variables to prevent scope conflicts.
Credentials must be resolved at runtime from a secret store and never stored in version-controlled files.
Managed configuration must be applied before project-scope configuration is read.

questions.explanation: Secrets must be resolved at runtime from a secret store and never written into version-controlled configuration files. The other options describe configuration precedence rules, which are not what was violated.

questions.question: An engineering organization is adopting Claude Code across 200 developers. A team lead has proposed that AI-generated pull requests bypass the standard code review process for changes under 50 lines, on the grounds that small changes are low-risk and review capacity is constrained. Which two Diligence-competency objections should you raise? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Code review capacity should be expanded to handle every code change submitted across the team.
The 50-line threshold should be raised to 200 lines instead to capture more changes overall.
Line count is a poor proxy for the actual risk a code change introduces into the system.
Removing review removes the verification mechanism that AI-generated output requires across the workflow.
AI-generated pull requests should be rejected as a default policy across the engineering organization.

questions.explanation: Line count is a weak proxy for risk — a two-line change to auth or a migration can be severe (C) — and removing review removes the verification step that AI-generated output specifically requires (D). A, B and E are impractical or unrelated policy positions rather than diligence objections.

questions.question: A technical team is cataloging risks specific to Claude's use in a document-grounded Q&A system. Which two items represent failure modes that are intrinsic to LLM-based systems rather than generic software defects? (Choose two.)

options.text: the model generating a plausible-sounding answer that is unsupported by any retrieved document
the model refusing a legitimate query because surface features triggered an overly broad safety pattern
an expired TLS certificate blocking outbound API calls to the Claude endpoint
a database connection timeout causing a retrieval call to return an empty result set
a misconfigured load balancer routing requests to a deprecated API version

questions.explanation: Plausible but unsupported output (A) and over-broad refusal of a legitimate query (B) are probabilistic model behaviours with no deterministic-software analogue. C, D and E are ordinary infrastructure faults.

questions.question: You are evaluating a Claude-based deployment for adherence to a specific regulation. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE mapping deployment data flows to specific regulatory clauses? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Compare the in-place controls against the regulatory requirements to identify any compliance gaps.
Inventory the vendor-provided compliance tooling and confirm which compliance affordances are in place.
Identify the applicability of the regulation based on data types, jurisdiction, and audience.
Document the identified gaps along with recommended remediations and residual risk for sign-off.
Schedule the remediation work with the engineering team based on the prioritized gap findings.

questions.explanation: Before mapping data flows to clauses you must establish that the regulation applies, based on data types, jurisdiction and audience (C), and inventory the vendor-provided compliance affordances already in place (B). A, D and E follow the mapping step.

questions.question: You are reviewing an integration specification for security gaps. Which two findings constitute valid security gaps in the specification? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Tool inputs and outputs are encrypted in transit using transport layer security between services.
Service credentials are placed in the prompt context where they can leak into logs and traces.
Tool calls execute server-side under a least-privilege service principal scoped to the requested action.
Role-based access control (RBAC) is enforced only at the response-rendering layer after the model accesses restricted data.
Per-user OAuth tokens are exchanged with scope-restricted permissions and refreshed within the active session.

questions.explanation: Credentials in the prompt context (B) leak into logs, traces and model output. RBAC enforced only at rendering (D) means restricted data already entered the model context, so the control is applied too late. A, C and E describe sound controls.

questions.question: You are running a risk assessment on a planned Claude-based deployment and must complete the inventory steps before assessing threats against assets. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE assessing threats against assets to estimate likelihood and impact? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Recommend mitigations and residual-risk acceptance for the risks that remain after analysis.
Document the assessment outcome with risks, mitigations, residual risk, and acceptance owners.
Enumerate the threat actors and attack vectors that are relevant to the deployment.
Identify the assets that the deployment touches along with the sensitivity of each asset.
Recommend mitigations and residual-risk acceptance for risks that remain.

questions.explanation: Threat-likelihood and impact assessment needs both sides of the inventory first: the assets touched and their sensitivity (D), and the relevant threat actors and attack vectors (C). A, B and E are downstream outputs.

questions.question: You are a platform architect designing an internal Claude-based assistant that serves both finance analysts and external auditors. Each population must access only documents permitted by their role. Where should role-based access control be enforced in the pipeline?

options.text: at the retrieval layer, before any role-restricted content reaches the prompt construction step or the model
after the response is generated, by post-filtering content that should not have been retrieved
nowhere in the pipeline; rely on the model's general refusal behavior to reject unauthorized document access without any enforced access control
inside the system prompt as a natural-language instruction for Claude to ignore unauthorized documents

questions.explanation: Enforce RBAC at the retrieval layer so unauthorised content never enters the prompt or the model context. Post-filtering (B) means the data was already exposed to the model, and prompt instructions (D) or reliance on refusal behaviour (C) are not enforcement.

questions.question: A customer support team has proposed delegating customer refund decisions to a Claude-driven workflow with no human review for refunds under 50 USD. The team's reasoning is that small refunds are low-risk and human review would erase the efficiency gain. Which Delegation-competency principle should guide your response?

options.text: Delegation scope should reflect the type of risk involved, not the transaction size alone.
Delegation scope should be set primarily by maximizing efficiency gains across the workflow.
Delegation should always include human review on every decision the workflow produces.
Delegation should be avoided entirely wherever financial transactions occur in the workflow.

questions.explanation: Delegation scope should track the type and reversibility of the risk, not the dollar amount; small refunds can still carry fraud, compliance and precedent risk. B optimises only for efficiency, C and D are absolutes that ignore risk tiering.

questions.question: A research summarization assistant has been deployed for six months. A user has flagged that a generated summary contained a fabricated citation. The product team has asked whether the incident requires architectural action or whether it is an isolated case. Which two Diligence-competency actions should you take? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Sample recent summaries to estimate the fabrication frequency across the population.
Treat the incident as an anecdotal isolated case and take no further investigative action.
Review whether citation grounding controls exist anywhere in the current generation pipeline.
Disable the assistant immediately for all current users without any prior diagnostic analysis.
Communicate to users that the assistant does not fabricate output as a matter of design.

questions.explanation: Establish frequency by sampling recent summaries (A) and determine whether citation grounding controls exist anywhere in the pipeline (C). B assumes the answer, D is disproportionate before diagnosis, E asserts something untrue.

questions.question: You are assessing data-exfiltration risk in a Claude-based assistant that has tools for both internal-document retrieval and outbound HTTP calls. Which scenario most directly indicates a data-exfiltration risk?

options.text: The outbound HTTP tool returns a 200 response when the assistant calls an allow-listed domain to fulfill a user-initiated data lookup request.
Adversarial content in retrieved documents instructs the model to call the outbound HTTP tool and send sensitive content to an attacker-controlled URL.
The user types a routine question into the assistant and receives a routine answer.
The internal-document retrieval tool returns a document that the user has authorization to view.

questions.explanation: Indirect prompt injection in retrieved content that drives an outbound HTTP call to an attacker-controlled URL is the classic exfiltration path: untrusted input plus an egress-capable tool. A, C and D describe normal authorised behaviour.

questions.question: You are defining escalation criteria for ambiguous cases in an automated workflow. Which set of criteria best supports consistent escalation?

options.text: confidence threshold below a defined level, presence of high-impact decision categories, ambiguity flags raised by content classifiers, and the user's explicit request for review
escalation at the discretion of whoever is available when the teams on-call engineer has spare capacity, with no defined threshold, category, or ambiguity criterion to trigger it
escalation only after an affected customer has already contacted the support channel to complain, by which point the automated workflow has already completed without human review
no escalation criteria at all; the model itself decides on each turn whether to escalate, without explicit confidence thresholds, impact categories, or classifier-based ambiguity flags

questions.explanation: Consistent escalation needs explicit, testable triggers: a confidence threshold, defined high-impact categories, classifier-raised ambiguity flags, and the user's own request for review. B, C and D leave escalation undefined, too late, or entirely to model discretion.

questions.question: A Claude architect observes that after a recent model-version upgrade, grounded responses began including claims not supported by the retrieved source documents. Which mitigation is most directly targeted at this failure mode?

options.text: replacing the shared API key with per-user OAuth tokens to restrict data access
scoring each new model version against a stable adversarial evaluation set
constraining responses to source-supported content combined with required citations and a verification step
treating retrieved data as untrusted and applying input classifiers at ingestion time

questions.explanation: The failure is ungrounded claims, so constrain responses to source-supported content, require citations and add a verification step. B detects drift but does not prevent it, A and D address access control and injection.

questions.question: You are preparing a HIPAA-eligible deployment for a healthcare customer. Which configuration supports HIPAA compliance using Anthropic-offered tools?

options.text: disabling all audit logging so that no PHI is recorded in any log store, on the assumption that the absence of logs satisfies HIPAA requirements without a signed BAA
an ad-hoc personal Claude account used by individual clinicians for PHI-related tasks, with no Business Associate Agreement, no Zero Data Retention, and no audit logging configured
Claude Enterprise with a signed Business Associate Agreement, Zero Data Retention enabled, and audit logging configured for compliance tracking
Claude Free with no contractual addendum, since consumer products meet HIPAA requirements out of the box

questions.explanation: HIPAA-eligible use requires an enterprise agreement with a signed BAA, Zero Data Retention, and audit logging for compliance tracking. A confuses absence of logs with compliance, B and D use consumer tiers with no contractual basis.

questions.question: You are auditing a procurement-assistant agent whose defined responsibility is to draft purchase requests for review. For each tool currently configured on the agent, select yes if the tool should remain after a least-privilege audit. Otherwise, select no if it should be removed.

statements.text: a read-only catalog lookup tool that returns vendor and SKU information
an inbox-send tool that emails purchase requests to vendors directly
a draft-write tool that creates purchase-request drafts in the review queue
a production-database admin tool unrelated to procurement
A read-only policy-document tool that returns the relevant procurement policies

questions.explanation: Yes - read-only catalog lookup supplies the vendor and SKU data a draft request needs and carries no write authority. No - emailing requests to vendors directly is an outbound, externally visible action that bypasses the human review the agent's scope depends on; sending belongs after approval, not to the drafting agent. Yes - writing drafts into the review queue is precisely the agent's defined responsibility and is the one write it should hold. No - a production-database admin tool is outside procurement scope entirely and grants privileges no defined task requires, making it the clearest removal. Yes - read-only policy lookup grounds the draft in current procurement rules with no write surface.

questions.question: You are defining transparency practices for a customer-facing assistant whose responses are materially shaped by AI. Which transparency practice most directly supports responsible deployment?

options.text: Disclose AI involvement only to internal staff and operators while withholding that information from the end users whose interactions are materially shaped by the AI system.
Refuse to answer any user question about how the responses were produced or whether AI was involved, treating the AI's role as confidential operational information.
Misrepresent the AI's role in producing responses in order to make the assistant feel more trustworthy or more human, undermining informed user consent and organizational transparency.
Disclose AI involvement to end users in line with the organization's transparency policy and provide a documented path to reach a human when needed.

questions.explanation: Disclose AI involvement to end users per the organisation's transparency policy and provide a documented route to a human. A withholds it from the affected users, B refuses legitimate questions, C is misrepresentation.

questions.question: A security team is evaluating two proposed controls. Control A adds an outbound tool allow-list with destination restrictions and per-call review. Control B scores responses against a stable adversarial evaluation set after each model-version change. Which two risk categories are correctly matched to these controls? (Choose two.)

options.text: Control A --> silent quality drift after a model-version upgrade
Control A --> data exfiltration via outbound tool calls
Control A --> prompt injection from adversarial content in retrieved data
Control B --> silent quality drift after a model-version upgrade
Control B --> data exfiltration via outbound tool calls

questions.explanation: An outbound allow-list with destination restrictions and per-call review directly limits data exfiltration through tool calls (B). Scoring each model version against a stable adversarial set detects silent quality drift (D). The other pairings mismatch control to risk.

questions.question: You are supporting an EU-based deployment with GDPR obligations. Which combination of measures best supports the deployment's GDPR posture?

options.text: disabling all data-retention configuration, redaction controls, and data-subject-rights handling to simplify day-to-day operations, accepting the resulting GDPR compliance exposure

enterprise-tier deployment with a signed Data Processing Addendum, defined data-retention configuration, redaction of personal data not needed for the task, and documented data-subject-rights handling
pasting full EU personal data into every prompt to "give Claude complete context" without considering purpose limitation, data minimization, or the organization's Data Processing Addendum obligations
using a personal Claude account tier for processing EU personal data at scale, with no signed Data Processing Addendum and no documented data-subject-rights handling procedure

questions.explanation: GDPR posture is supported by an enterprise tier with a signed DPA, defined retention configuration, redaction of personal data not needed for the task (data minimisation and purpose limitation), and documented data-subject-rights handling. A, C and D each remove one or more of those requirements.

questions.question: You are configuring tool permissions for a Claude-based assistant. The assistant's defined responsibilities require read access to a knowledge base and write access to a draft queue, and nothing else. Which scoping design best applies least privilege?

options.text: Allow access to all tools with read permissions globally and restrict write permissions to the draft-queue tool, without scoping to only the specific tools required for defined tasks.
Per-role allow-list of exactly the read-knowledge-base and write-draft-queue tools, enforced at the orchestration layer.
Allow access to every tool in the catalog and rely on the model to decline tools it should not use.
Disable all tools entirely to achieve a minimal permission surface, accepting that the assistant can no longer perform the read-knowledge base or write-draft-queue tasks it was designed for.

questions.explanation: Least privilege means a per-role allow-list containing exactly the two required tools, enforced at the orchestration layer rather than left to model discretion. A over-grants reads, C relies on the model to police itself, D disables the required capability.

questions.question: A Claude architect is implementing safety controls for a customer-facing advice assistant that must never provide regulated investment recommendations. Which two guardrail implementations most directly enforce this constraint? (Choose two.)

options.text: Log all user queries to a SIEM for post-hoc compliance review.
Limit session length to reduce the volume of queries processed per user per day.
Add an output classifier that detects and blocks responses containing regulated investment-recommendation language.
Define explicit out-of-scope categories in the system prompt with fixed refusal phrasing for investment advice requests.
Increase response temperature to introduce variability that reduces the likelihood of specific recommendations.

questions.explanation: Two complementary layers: explicit out-of-scope categories with fixed refusal phrasing in the system prompt (D), and an output classifier that blocks regulated investment-recommendation language before it reaches the user (C). A is post-hoc, B and E do not constrain content.

questions.question: When communicating an architectural decision to a security and compliance reviewer, which content set is most aligned with that audience's primary concerns?

options.text: implementation timeline, component interfaces, and deployment sequence for the engineering team
feature delivery schedule, roadmap dependencies, and scope boundaries for the product manager
decision rationale, business outcomes, and high-level risk summary for executive review
threat model, control mappings, residual-risk acceptance criteria, and audit traceability

questions.explanation: Security and compliance reviewers need the threat model, mapping of controls to requirements, residual-risk acceptance criteria, and audit traceability. The other sets target engineering, product and executive audiences.

questions.question: During an architectural review, the security team identifies a risk that adversarial content injected into retrieved documents could manipulate the model's behavior. Which mitigation most directly addresses this threat?

options.text: Score outputs against a stable adversarial evaluation set on each model-version change.
Restrict outbound tool calls to an approved destination allow-list.
Treat all retrieved content as untrusted input and apply input classifiers with output validation.
Require citations for each claim and constrain responses to source-supported content.

questions.explanation: Indirect prompt injection is mitigated by treating all retrieved content as untrusted input, screening it with input classifiers and validating the resulting output. B limits the exfiltration path, D addresses grounding, A addresses drift.

questions.question: You are compiling guardrail tactics for a customer-facing assistant. Which two tactics belong on the guardrail list? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Embed approved override phrases that let trusted users relax guardrails on demand.
Layer prompt-level guardrails with runtime content checks rather than relying on either alone.
Validate the model output against a structured schema before downstream actions are taken.
Lower sampling temperature globally to reduce the chance of off-policy completions.
Rely on a single hardened system prompt that enumerates every disallowed behavior.

questions.explanation: Defence in depth: layer prompt-level guardrails with runtime content checks rather than relying on either alone (B), and validate model output against a structured schema before any downstream action executes (C). A builds in a bypass, D is a sampling knob, E is single-layer.

questions.question: The compliance team at a firm has approved a Claude Skill that generates client-facing investment summaries. The Skill includes the firm's required disclaimers and prohibited-language list. A product manager has asked whether additional guardrails are needed at the application layer or whether the Skill alone is sufficient. Which two guardrail responsibilities should remain at the application layer rather than the Skill? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Apply the disclaimer template that the compliance team has standardized firm-wide.
Format output sections according to the firm's standardized house style guidelines.
Apply the prohibited-language list that the compliance team maintains and updates.
Log every generated summary to the firm's compliance audit trail for retention.
Verify the requesting user is authorized to generate investment summaries at all.

questions.explanation: Authorisation of the requesting user (E) and audit-trail logging of every generated summary (D) must be enforced by the application, since a Skill is instruction content the model follows and cannot itself guarantee identity checks or durable logging. A, B and C are exactly the standardised content the Skill carries.

questions.question: A security audit uncovers two issues: (1) all end users share a single API key, and (2) tool calls are executed without logging the initiating user. Which two mitigations directly address these specific findings? (Choose two.)

options.text: Replace the shared API key with per-user OAuth tokens carrying scope-restricted permissions.
Validate structured outputs against a schema before downstream actions are executed.
Move credentials out of the prompt context and resolve them from a server-side secret store.
Enforce RBAC at the retrieval layer before content enters the model context.
Add actor attribution to tool-call logs so each call records the initiating user identity.

questions.explanation: Per-user OAuth tokens with scope-restricted permissions replace the shared key (A), and actor attribution on tool-call logs records the initiating user (E). B, C and D are sound controls but address other findings.

questions.question: A Claude architect is designing a HIPAA-compliant pipeline that processes patient records. Which two design decisions directly support HIPAA compliance requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: setting max tokens to a low value to minimize the volume of text generated per request
enforcing role-based access controls so that PHI is retrievable only by authorized personnel
selecting the highest-capability Claude model to maximize diagnostic accuracy
ensuring patient data is never included in training feedback loops sent to the model provider without a BAA in place
using streaming responses to reduce perceived latency for clinical users

questions.explanation: RBAC so PHI is retrievable only by authorised personnel (B), and ensuring patient data never enters provider-side training or feedback loops without a BAA (D). A, C and E are performance or quality choices with no HIPAA bearing.

questions.question: You are designing a human-in-the-loop validation workflow for a new Claude-based deployment and must complete the design steps before piloting the workflow. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE piloting the workflow with a representative subset of traffic? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Onboard the reviewer pool with role-specific training on the check criteria and escalation procedures.
Iterate the workflow design based on observed pilot findings before broader rollout to production.
Document the workflow with check criteria, escalation paths, and service-level agreements (SLAs) for each step.
Define the sampling strategy and the escalation criteria at each oversight point in the pipeline.
Identify the decision points in the pipeline that require human oversight by impact and reversibility.

questions.explanation: Design precedes pilot: identify the decision points needing oversight by impact and reversibility (E), then define the sampling strategy and escalation criteria at each of those points (D). A, B and C follow that design work.

questions.question: You are responding to an adversarial input pattern in which users include text claiming admin authority and instructing the model to bypass safety restrictions. Which combination of controls most effectively mitigates this attack pattern?

options.text: granting users any privilege level they assert in their message content, on the assumption that cooperative behavior requires honoring self-declared authority without independent verification

prompt-level instructions that treat user content as untrusted data, runtime classifiers that detect override attempts, scoped tool permissions that cannot be elevated by user content, and audit logging of attempts
trusting that the model will intrinsically recognize and reject all bypass attempts without prompt-level instructions, runtime classifiers, scoped permissions, or audit logging
